relations.note: Khnum is Heqet’s partner or consort, especially at Herwer.

relations.myth: Formation and animation of Hatshepsut and her ka
relations.note: Khnum fashions Hatshepsut and her ka while Heqet supplies life.
Heqet and Khnum lead the pregnant Queen Ahmose toward delivery.

relations.myth: Birth of Reddjedet’s three royal sons
relations.note: Khnum travels with Heqet’s birth team, carries baggage, and grants health.

relations.myth: Birth of Reddjedet’s three royal sons
relations.note: Isis addresses each child while Heqet hastens the delivery.

relations.myth: Birth of Reddjedet’s three royal sons
relations.note: Nephthys stands behind Reddjedet while Heqet hastens each birth.

relations.myth: Birth of Reddjedet’s three royal sons
relations.note: Meskhenet proclaims each newborn’s destiny after Heqet hastens delivery.

relations.myth: Birth of Reddjedet’s three royal sons
relations.note: Re commissions Heqet and four other deities to deliver the triplets.
Heqet’s generative power accompanies the gathering of Osiris’s bones.
Frog-form Heqet appears near Osiris’s bier within renewal imagery.
Khepri and Heqet share four ritual basins associated with transition.

relations.myth: Formation of the divine royal child
relations.note: Heqet extends the ankh, giving or mediating life to Hatshepsut.

relations.myth: Divine conception and formation of Hatshepsut
relations.note: Amun fathers Hatshepsut in the birth cycle where Heqet supplies life.
Local Qus theology presents Haroeris as born from Heqet.

relations.myth: Formation of the child god Ihy
relations.note: Heqet assists Khnum in forming Ihy but is not necessarily his mother.
Later theology treats Hathor as Heqet’s functional equivalent or substitute.
A late Hermopolitan arrangement can make Heqet Thoth’s partner.
